children: on Saturday suggested a silver lining to an apparent hack of the FBI’s National Criminal Information Center (NCIC), saying the breach could potentially reveal information about alleged voter fraud.
This is the second intrusion into the bureau’s systems in recent years.
Trump Sees Upside in FBI Database Hack
In an interview with Fox News, Trump said, “Maybe we’ll learn about the voter fraud, all the voter fraud that took place.” He added, “I always like to put things on a positive spin.”
Law-enforcement agencies use the system to share criminal justice information, including records related to wanted persons and other law-enforcement matters.

Hackers reportedly accessed the NCIC, which contains a range of law-enforcement records, including information related to wanted persons, missing persons and fingerprint records, MS NOW reported, citing sources.

Access to the system is restricted to authorized law-enforcement personnel, although the database is not classified. It remains unclear whether hackers extracted any data or what information may have been compromised.
Trump Links Breach to Russia Probe, Names No Suspect

Trump also suggested the intrusion could shed light on the Russia investigation. “Wouldn’t it be great to learn about Russia, Russia, Russia?” he said. “People should hear about it, because it actually put our country in danger, and so maybe we’ll learn things that we wouldn’t have learned otherwise.”
Trump did not identify a suspect or provide evidence linking the breach to a specific individual, group or country.
Second FBI Cyber Incident Since September

In September, the FBI investigated claims by a hacking group known as ShinyHunters that it had breached FBIJobs.gov and stolen sensitive personal information belonging to thousands of bureau employees and job applicants. The FBI said it was investigating the alleged breach, while the group’s claims of data theft were not fully independently verified. The recruitment portal was taken offline during the investigation.
